Independent Constraint Generation (ICG) bypasses trace-constraint coupling by generating constraints directly from the problem statement, producing near-zero average effect ($\Delta = -1.96$\,pp and $+1.47$\,pp across two FOLIO seeds; $-0.50$\,pp on LogiQA; McNemar $p = .206$, n.s.). Contrastive scoring generates pro and con constraints for each candidate but yields $\Delta = -9.31$\,pp on FOLIO ($p < 0.01$) and $-4.50$\,pp on LogiQA ($p = .160$, n.s.), with ${\sim}$21\% degenerate scores on both datasets. Debate adds a proposer-critic-defense chain, producing $\Delta = -18.63$\,pp on FOLIO and $-23.00$\,pp on LogiQA, both statistically significant by McNemar's test ($p < 0.001$ on both datasets). Discordant-pair analysis reveals the asymmetry: on FOLIO, 60 questions flipped from correct to wrong versus only 22 from wrong to correct; on LogiQA, 64 versus 18. The method actively destroys SC's correct predictions rather than introducing balanced noise. Three of five method-dataset conditions reach significance, confirming that degradation is systematic, not stochastic. At the 7B scale, multi-role prompting adds cognitive overhead that degrades both reasoning and extraction quality.

1	\section{Discussion}
2	\label{sec:discussion}
3	
4	The oracle experiments causally identify the failure source. Holding all pipeline components fixed and varying only constraint source, gold annotations yield $+14.22$\,pp on FOLIO and $+11.50$\,pp on ProofWriter ($p < 0.001$), while the best self-extraction captures only 24.1\% of this ceiling. Because the aggregation mechanism is identical in both conditions, the gap localizes entirely to extraction quality.
5	
6	Trace correlation affects SICA through two channels. The \emph{direct} channel limits voting diversity: Eff-$K < 2$ for many conditions (Table~\ref{tab:independence}) confirms that same-model traces violate the CJT independence requirement, explaining the SC plateau. The \emph{indirect} channel operates through constraint quality: correlated traces produce homogeneous constraints, causing MAX-SAT to degenerate to vote counting (Appendix~\ref{app:ablation}). The oracle result disambiguates: gold constraints applied to the same correlated traces yield $+14.22$\,pp, proving that constraint homogenization---not voting diversity---is the proximal bottleneck.
7	
8	\paragraph{The independence-accuracy trade-off.} The $\kappa$ generalization analysis (\S\ref{sec:remediation}) constitutes the primary finding of this paper. Diverse-Prompt achieves $\kappa = 0.40$ ($\approx$ SC's $0.44$): prompt variation does not break the correlation. Debate reduces $\kappa$ to 0.15 (Eff-$K = 4.44$) but collapses accuracy by $-18.6$\,pp on FOLIO and $-23.0$\,pp on LogiQA. This independence-accuracy trade-off is a fundamental Pareto frontier: methods that increase trace independence necessarily degrade accuracy, while methods that preserve accuracy cannot break the correlation floor. Crucially, this trade-off constrains \emph{all} same-model trace aggregation methods---not only symbolic approaches---because it arises from the model's output distribution, not from any specific aggregation procedure. Published systems that report positive results---DyLoS \citep{xu2026dylos}, Aristotle \citep{li2025aristotle}, FoVer \citep{wang2025fover}, Logic-LM \citep{pan2023logiclm}---each bypass same-model self-extraction, trading simplicity for architectures that introduce genuinely independent signal.
9	
10	\paragraph{Diagnostic tools for practitioners.} Our analysis yields two zero-cost diagnostics applicable before any constraint extraction. First, $C_0$ combined with SC accuracy predicts when symbolic augmentation is unlikely to help: $C_0 < 5\%$ implies degeneration; SC $\geq 60\%$ implies confirmation bias; SC $\leq 40\%$ implies error amplification. Second, the $\kappa$-based Eff-$K$ metric quantifies SC's own scaling ceiling: at Eff-$K \approx 2$ (typical at $K = 12$), additional traces add negligible independent information regardless of aggregation method.
11	
12	\paragraph{Statistical evidence.} No positive SICA effect reaches $p < 0.05$. The four-seed replication yields $p = 0.092$, $0.070$, $1.0$, and $1.0$. In contrast, negative effects are significant: $\Delta = -2.83$\,pp ($p = 0.014$) and $-2.50$\,pp ($p = 0.011$). Oracle controls remain highly significant ($p < 0.001$). The converging evidence rests on the pattern across analyses, not any single $p$-value.
13	
14	\paragraph{Scale limitations and future work.} The method-level interventions that test the trade-off most directly use Mistral-7B. At the 7B scale, Debate may impose cognitive overhead that larger models can absorb; whether 14B+ or 70B+ models shift the Pareto frontier is an open question. The trade-off itself is fundamental---it follows from the correlation structure of same-model outputs---but its severity may vary with scale. Three paths forward trade simplicity for independence: trained extractors, external provers, and multi-model pipelines.

\section{Discussion}
\label{sec:discussion}

The oracle experiments causally identify the failure source. Holding all pipeline components fixed and varying only constraint source, gold annotations yield $+14.22$\,pp on FOLIO and $+11.50$\,pp on ProofWriter ($p < 0.001$), while the best self-extraction captures only 24.1\% of this ceiling. Because the aggregation mechanism is identical in both conditions, the gap localizes entirely to extraction quality.

Trace correlation affects SICA through two channels. The \emph{direct} channel limits voting diversity: Eff-$K < 2$ for many conditions (Table~\ref{tab:independence}) confirms that same-model traces violate the CJT independence requirement, explaining the SC plateau. The \emph{indirect} channel operates through constraint quality: correlated traces produce homogeneous constraints, causing MAX-SAT to degenerate to vote counting (Appendix~\ref{app:ablation}). The oracle result disambiguates: gold constraints applied to the same correlated traces yield $+14.22$\,pp, proving that constraint homogenization---not voting diversity---is the proximal bottleneck.

\paragraph{The independence-accuracy trade-off.} The $\kappa$ generalization analysis (\S\ref{sec:remediation}) constitutes the primary finding of this paper. Diverse-Prompt achieves $\kappa = 0.40$ ($\approx$ SC's $0.44$): prompt variation does not break the correlation. Debate reduces $\kappa$ to 0.15 (Eff-$K = 4.44$) but collapses accuracy by $-18.6$\,pp on FOLIO and $-23.0$\,pp on LogiQA. This independence-accuracy trade-off is a fundamental Pareto frontier: methods that increase trace independence necessarily degrade accuracy, while methods that preserve accuracy cannot break the correlation floor. Crucially, this trade-off constrains \emph{all} same-model trace aggregation methods---not only symbolic approaches---because it arises from the model's output distribution, not from any specific aggregation procedure. Published systems that report positive results---DyLoS \citep{xu2026dylos}, Aristotle \citep{li2025aristotle}, FoVer \citep{wang2025fover}, Logic-LM \citep{pan2023logiclm}---each bypass same-model self-extraction, trading simplicity for architectures that introduce genuinely independent signal.

\paragraph{Diagnostic tools for practitioners.} Our analysis yields two zero-cost diagnostics applicable before any constraint extraction. First, $C_0$ combined with SC accuracy predicts when symbolic augmentation is unlikely to help: $C_0 < 5\%$ implies degeneration; SC $\geq 60\%$ implies confirmation bias; SC $\leq 40\%$ implies error amplification. Second, the $\kappa$-based Eff-$K$ metric quantifies SC's own scaling ceiling: at Eff-$K \approx 2$ (typical at $K = 12$), additional traces add negligible independent information regardless of aggregation method.

\paragraph{Statistical evidence.} No positive SICA effect reaches $p < 0.05$. The four-seed replication yields $p = 0.092$, $0.070$, $1.0$, and $1.0$. In contrast, negative effects are significant: $\Delta = -2.83$\,pp ($p = 0.014$) and $-2.50$\,pp ($p = 0.011$). Oracle controls remain highly significant ($p < 0.001$). The converging evidence rests on the pattern across analyses, not any single $p$-value.

\paragraph{Scale limitations and future work.} The method-level interventions that test the trade-off most directly use Mistral-7B. At the 7B scale, Debate may impose cognitive overhead that larger models can absorb; whether 14B+ or 70B+ models shift the Pareto frontier is an open question. The trade-off itself is fundamental---it follows from the correlation structure of same-model outputs---but its severity may vary with scale. Three paths forward trade simplicity for independence: trained extractors, external provers, and multi-model pipelines.

50	\paragraph{Method-level interventions.} Three method-level strategies target different aspects of the independence bottleneck on Mistral-7B (Table~\ref{tab:method_interventions}). Independent Constraint Generation (ICG) bypasses trace-constraint coupling by generating constraints directly from the problem statement, producing near-zero average effect ($\Delta = -1.96$\,pp and $+1.47$\,pp across two FOLIO seeds; $-0.50$\,pp on LogiQA; McNemar $p = .206$, n.s.). Contrastive scoring generates pro and con constraints for each candidate but yields $\Delta = -9.31$\,pp on FOLIO ($p < 0.01$) and $-4.50$\,pp on LogiQA ($p = .160$, n.s.), with ${\sim}$21\% degenerate scores on both datasets. Debate adds a proposer-critic-defense chain, producing $\Delta = -18.63$\,pp on FOLIO and $-23.00$\,pp on LogiQA, both statistically significant by McNemar's test ($p < 0.001$ on both datasets). Discordant-pair analysis reveals the asymmetry: on FOLIO, 60 questions flipped from correct to wrong versus only 22 from wrong to correct; on LogiQA, 64 versus 18. The method actively destroys SC's correct predictions rather than introducing balanced noise. Three of five method-dataset conditions reach significance, confirming that degradation is systematic, not stochastic. At the 7B scale, multi-role prompting adds cognitive overhead that degrades both reasoning and extraction quality.

1	\section{Discussion}
2	\label{sec:discussion}
3	
4	The oracle experiments causally identify the failure source. Holding all pipeline components fixed and varying only constraint source, gold annotations yield $+14.22$\,pp on FOLIO and $+11.50$\,pp on ProofWriter ($p < 0.001$), while the best self-extraction captures only 24.1\% of this ceiling. Because the aggregation mechanism is identical in both conditions, the gap localizes entirely to extraction quality.
5	
6	Trace correlation affects SICA through two channels. The \emph{direct} channel limits voting diversity: Eff-$K < 2$ for many conditions (Table~\ref{tab:independence}) confirms that same-model traces violate the CJT independence requirement, explaining the SC plateau. The \emph{indirect} channel operates through constraint quality: correlated traces produce homogeneous constraints, causing MAX-SAT to degenerate to vote counting (Appendix~\ref{app:ablation}). The oracle result disambiguates: gold constraints applied to the same correlated traces yield $+14.22$\,pp, proving that constraint homogenization---not voting diversity---is the proximal bottleneck.
7	
8	\paragraph{The independence-accuracy trade-off.} The $\kappa$ generalization analysis (\S\ref{sec:remediation}) constitutes the primary finding of this paper. Diverse-Prompt achieves $\kappa = 0.40$ ($\approx$ SC's $0.44$): prompt variation does not break the correlation. Debate reduces $\kappa$ to 0.15 (Eff-$K = 4.44$) but collapses accuracy by $-18.6$\,pp on FOLIO and $-23.0$\,pp on LogiQA. This independence-accuracy trade-off is a fundamental Pareto frontier: methods that increase trace independence necessarily degrade accuracy, while methods that preserve accuracy cannot break the correlation floor. Crucially, this trade-off constrains \emph{all} same-model trace aggregation methods---not only symbolic approaches---because it arises from the model's output distribution, not from any specific aggregation procedure. Published systems that report positive results---DyLoS \citep{xu2026dylos}, Aristotle \citep{li2025aristotle}, FoVer \citep{wang2025fover}, Logic-LM \citep{pan2023logiclm}---each bypass same-model self-extraction, trading simplicity for architectures that introduce genuinely independent signal.
9	
10	\paragraph{Diagnostic tools for practitioners.} Our analysis yields two zero-cost diagnostics applicable before any constraint extraction. First, $C_0$ combined with SC accuracy predicts when symbolic augmentation is unlikely to help: $C_0 < 5\%$ implies degeneration; SC $\geq 60\%$ implies confirmation bias; SC $\leq 40\%$ implies error amplification. Second, the $\kappa$-based Eff-$K$ metric quantifies SC's own scaling ceiling: at Eff-$K \approx 2$ (typical at $K = 12$), additional traces add negligible independent information regardless of aggregation method.
11	
12	\paragraph{Statistical evidence.} No positive SICA effect reaches $p < 0.05$. The four-seed replication yields $p = 0.092$, $0.070$, $1.0$, and $1.0$. In contrast, negative effects are significant: $\Delta = -2.83$\,pp ($p = 0.014$) and $-2.50$\,pp ($p = 0.011$). McNemar's paired test on method-level interventions confirms the pattern: three of five method-dataset conditions reach significance (Debate $p < 0.001$ on both datasets; Contrastive $p < 0.01$ on FOLIO), with discordant pairs heavily skewed toward correct$\to$wrong flips. Oracle controls remain highly significant ($p < 0.001$). The converging evidence rests on the pattern across analyses, not any single $p$-value.
13	
14	\paragraph{Scale limitations and future work.} The method-level interventions that test the trade-off most directly use Mistral-7B. At the 7B scale, Debate may impose cognitive overhead that larger models can absorb; whether 14B+ or 70B+ models shift the Pareto frontier is an open question. The trade-off itself is fundamental---it follows from the correlation structure of same-model outputs---but its severity may vary with scale. Three paths forward trade simplicity for independence: trained extractors, external provers, and multi-model pipelines.

Holding all pipeline components fixed and varying only constraint source, gold annotations yield $+14.22$\,pp on FOLIO and $+11.50$\,pp on ProofWriter ($p < 0.001$), while the best self-extraction captures only 24.1\% of this ceiling. Because the aggregation mechanism is identical in both conditions, the gap localizes entirely to extraction quality.

Trace correlation affects SICA through two channels. The \emph{direct} channel limits voting diversity: Eff-$K < 2$ for many conditions (Table~\ref{tab:independence}) confirms that same-model traces violate the CJT independence requirement, explaining the SC plateau. The \emph{indirect} channel operates through constraint quality: correlated traces produce homogeneous constraints, causing MAX-SAT to degenerate to vote counting (Appendix~\ref{app:ablation}). The oracle result disambiguates: gold constraints applied to the same correlated traces yield $+14.22$\,pp, proving that constraint homogenization---not voting diversity---is the proximal bottleneck.

Diverse-Prompt achieves $\kappa = 0.40$ ($\approx$ SC's $0.44$): prompt variation does not break the correlation. Debate reduces $\kappa$ to 0.15 (Eff-$K = 4.44$) but collapses accuracy by $-18.6$\,pp on FOLIO and $-23.0$\,pp on LogiQA. Published systems that report positive results---DyLoS \citep{xu2026dylos}, Aristotle \citep{li2025aristotle}, FoVer \citep{wang2025fover}, Logic-LM \citep{pan2023logiclm}---each bypass same-model self-extraction, trading simplicity for architectures that introduce genuinely independent signal.

First, $C_0$ combined with SC accuracy predicts when symbolic augmentation is unlikely to help: $C_0 < 5\%$ implies degeneration; SC $\geq 60\%$ implies confirmation bias; SC $\leq 40\%$ implies error amplification. Oracle controls remain highly significant ($p < 0.001$). The converging evidence rests on the pattern across analyses, not any single $p$-value.

\paragraph{Scale limitations and future work.} The method-level interventions that test the trade-off most directly use Mistral-7B. At the 7B scale, Debate may impose cognitive overhead that larger models can absorb; whether 14B+ or 70B+ models shift the Pareto frontier is an open question. The trade-off itself is fundamental---it follows from the correlation structure of same-model outputs---but its severity may vary with scale. Three paths forward trade simplicity for independence: trained extractors, external provers, and multi-model pipelines.

50	\paragraph{Method-level interventions.} Three method-level strategies target different aspects of the independence bottleneck on Mistral-7B (Table~\ref{tab:method_interventions}). Independent Constraint Generation (ICG) bypasses trace-constraint coupling by generating constraints directly from the problem statement, producing near-zero average effect ($\Delta = -1.96$\,pp and $+1.47$\,pp across two FOLIO seeds; $-0.50$\,pp on LogiQA; McNemar $p = .206$, n.s.). Contrastive scoring generates pro and con constraints for each candidate but yields $\Delta = -9.31$\,pp on FOLIO ($p < 0.01$) and $-4.50$\,pp on LogiQA ($p = .160$, n.s.), with ${\sim}$21\% degenerate scores on both datasets. Debate adds a proposer-critic-defense chain, producing $\Delta = -18.63$\,pp on FOLIO and $-23.00$\,pp on LogiQA, both statistically significant by McNemar's test ($p < 0.001$ on both datasets). Discordant-pair analysis reveals the asymmetry: on FOLIO, 60 questions flipped from correct to wrong versus only 22 from wrong to correct; on LogiQA, 64 versus 18. The method actively destroys SC's correct predictions rather than introducing balanced noise. Three of six method-dataset conditions reach significance, confirming that degradation is systematic, not stochastic. At the 7B scale, multi-role prompting adds cognitive overhead that degrades both reasoning and extraction quality.

1	
2	\section{Prompt Templates}
3	\label{app:prompts}
4	
5	SICA uses domain-specific prompt templates for constraint extraction: one for mathematical reasoning (GSM8K, AIME) and one for logical reasoning (ProofWriter, FOLIO). Both share the same system prompt. The LLM is called with temperature $T{=}0.3$, max tokens $1024$, and structured JSON output mode. Up to 6 traces are processed in parallel via thread pooling, with 2 retries on failure (exponential backoff, base 0.5s).
6	
7	\paragraph{System Prompt.}
8	
9	\begin{lstlisting}
10	You are a constraint extraction tool. Output ONLY
11	valid JSON. Do NOT solve problems, reason about
12	correctness, or think step-by-step. Extract
13	constraints from the given trace exactly as stated.
14	\end{lstlisting}
15	
16	\paragraph{Mathematical Constraint Extraction (EXTRACTION\_PROMPT).}
17	
18	Used for GSM8K and AIME datasets. The placeholder \texttt{\{trace\}} is replaced with the reasoning trace at runtime.
19	
20	\begin{lstlisting}
21	Extract mathematical constraints from this reasoning
22	trace as a JSON object.
23	
24	Rules:
25	- type: "equation", "inequality", or "predicate"
26	- expression: human-readable, e.g. "x + y == 14"
27	- z3_formula: a single comparison expression in
28	  Python Z3 syntax
29	- source_step: step number where the constraint
30	  appears
31	- Use variable names from the trace
32	
33	z3_formula MUST follow these rules:
34	- Allowed operators: ==, !=, <, >, <=, >=, +, -, *,
35	  /, **, %
36	- Use individual named variables: a1, a2, a3...
37	  NOT arrays a[1] or sets A
38	- Expand all sums explicitly:
39	  "a1 + a2 + a3 == 55" NOT "sum([a1,a2,a3])"
40	- NO Python builtins: sum(), len(), max(), min(),
41	  list(), set(), range(), int()
42	- Each z3_formula must be exactly ONE comparison
43	  (==, !=, <, >, <=, >=)
44	- For multiple values, write separate constraints
45	  for each
46	
47	Output ONLY the JSON below, nothing else:
48	{"constraints": [{"type": "equation",
49	  "expression": "x + y == 14",
50	  "z3_formula": "x + y == 14",
51	  "source_step": 1}],
52	 "answer": "final_answer",
53	 "variables": ["x", "y"]}
54	
55	Trace:
56	{trace}
57	\end{lstlisting}
58	
59	\paragraph{Logical Constraint Extraction (LOGIC\_EXTRACTION\_PROMPT).}
60	
61	Used for ProofWriter and FOLIO datasets.
62	
63	\begin{lstlisting}
64	IMPORTANT: You are an EXTRACTION tool, NOT a problem
65	solver.
66	- Do NOT re-solve or re-reason about the problem.
67	- Do NOT verify whether the trace's reasoning is
68	  correct.
69	- ONLY extract the logical constraints that are
70	  explicitly stated or used in the trace below.
71	- Output ONLY the JSON object, nothing else.
72	
73	Extract logical constraints from this reasoning trace
74	about a logic problem.
75	
76	The problem has facts (base assertions), rules
77	(grounded implications), and derived conclusions.
78	Convert each into a Z3 boolean formula.
79	
80	Variable naming:
81	- Unary property: property_entity
82	  (e.g., kind_anne, red_charlie, round_fiona)
83	- Binary relation: relation_subject_object
84	  (e.g., eats_bear_squirrel, likes_lion_cat)
85	- Use lowercase with underscores only
86	
87	Constraint types:
88	- "fact": a given assertion,
89	  e.g., kind_anne == True
90	- "rule": a grounded implication over specific
91	  entities, e.g., Implies(kind_anne, nice_anne)
92	- "derived": an inferred conclusion from facts +
93	  rules, e.g., nice_anne == True
94	
95	Z3 operators:
96	- Implies(a, b) for if-then rules
97	- And(a, b, ...) for conjunctive conditions
98	- Or(a, b, ...) for disjunctive conditions
99	- Not(a) for negation
100	- == True / == False for boolean assertions
101	
102	Output ONLY the JSON below, nothing else:
103	{"constraints": [{"type": "fact",
104	  "expression": "kind(anne)",
105	  "z3_formula": "kind_anne == True",
106	  "source_step": 1}],
107	 "answer": "True or False or Unknown",
108	 "variables": ["kind_anne"]}
109	
110	Trace:
111	{trace}

148	\section{Z3 MaxSAT Evaluation Pseudocode}
149	\label{app:z3-pseudocode}
150	
151	Algorithm~\ref{alg:maxsat} describes the Z3 MaxSAT solving procedure. Algorithm~\ref{alg:scorer} describes the source-trace attribution scoring.
152	
153	Domain constraint variables (e.g., \texttt{x + y == 14}) and answer assertion variables (e.g., \texttt{\_\_sica\_answer\_42 == True}) are logically independent in the Z3 formulation. Discriminative signal arises solely from conflicts among domain constraints: when traces supporting different answers produce mutually contradictory constraints, the solver excludes the lower-weight subset, and the scorer penalizes the corresponding answers.
154	
155	\begin{algorithm}[h]
156	\caption{Z3 Weighted Partial MAX-SAT}
157	\label{alg:maxsat}
158	\begin{algorithmic}[1]
159	\Require Deduplicated constraint set $\mathcal{C} = \{(c_m, w_m, S_m)\}_{m=1}^M$ where $c_m$ is a Z3 formula, $w_m$ is weight, $S_m$ is the set of source trace indices
160	\Ensure Partition $(\mathcal{C}^*, \mathcal{C}^{\setminus})$ where $\mathcal{C}^*$ is the max-weight satisfiable subset
161	\State $\textit{opt} \gets \textsc{Z3.Optimize()}$
162	\For{$m = 1, \ldots, M$}
163	    \State $b_m \gets$ fresh Boolean indicator
164	    \State $\textit{opt}.\textsc{Add}(b_m \Rightarrow c_m)$ \Comment{soft clause guarded by indicator}
165	    \State $\textit{opt}.\textsc{AddSoft}(b_m,\; \text{weight}=w_m)$
166	\EndFor
167	\State $\textit{result} \gets \textit{opt}.\textsc{Check}()$
168	\State $\textit{model} \gets \textit{opt}.\textsc{Model}()$
169	\State $\mathcal{C}^* \gets \{(c_m, w_m, S_m) : \textit{model}(b_m) = \top\}$
170	\State $\mathcal{C}^{\setminus} \gets \mathcal{C} \setminus \mathcal{C}^*$
171	\State \Return $(\mathcal{C}^*, \mathcal{C}^{\setminus})$
172	\end{algorithmic}
173	\end{algorithm}
174	
175	\begin{algorithm}[h]
176	\caption{Source-Trace Attribution Scoring}
177	\label{alg:scorer}
178	\begin{algorithmic}[1]
179	\Require Satisfied set $\mathcal{C}^*$, excluded set $\mathcal{C}^{\setminus}$, candidate answers $\mathcal{A}$, trace-answer mapping $\tau: \text{trace\_idx} \to a$, penalty weight $\alpha$
180	\Ensure Score $s(a)$ for each $a \in \mathcal{A}$
181	\For{each $a \in \mathcal{A}$}
182	    \State $T_a \gets \{i : \tau(i) = a\}$ \Comment{trace indices producing answer $a$}
183	    \State $\textit{pos}(a) \gets \sum_{(c,w,S) \in \mathcal{C}^*} w \cdot \mathbf{1}[S \cap T_a \neq \emptyset]$
184	    \State $\textit{neg}(a) \gets \sum_{(c,w,S) \in \mathcal{C}^{\setminus}} w \cdot \mathbf{1}[S \cap T_a \neq \emptyset]$
185	    \State $s(a) \gets \textit{pos}(a) - \alpha \cdot \textit{neg}(a)$
186	\EndFor
187	\State \Return $a^* = \arg\max_{a \in \mathcal{A}} s(a)$
188	\end{algorithmic}
189	\end{algorithm}

270	\section{Case Studies: Discordant Predictions}
271	\label{app:case-studies}
272	
273	Among 804 problems, SICA and SC agree on 773 (96.1\%). The 31 discordant cases comprise 16 SICA wins (SICA correct, SC wrong), 14 SC wins (SC correct, SICA wrong), and 1 where both select different wrong answers. All 31 occur at exact ties (entropy${=}1.0$, 6:6 vote split) or near-ties (entropy${\geq}0.9183$, 8:4 at most), since SICA can differ from SC only when constraint weights shift the majority away from SC's tiebreak choice. We present three representative cases that illustrate the mechanism behind capability trap failures.
274	
275	\paragraph{Case 1: SICA Wins (folio\_134, FOLIO).}
276	
277	\emph{Premises}: Some mammals have teeth. Platypus have no teeth. Platypus are mammals. Humans have teeth. \emph{Conclusion}: Humans are mammals. \emph{Gold}: Unknown.
278	
279	The premises state that \emph{some} mammals have teeth and that humans have teeth, but ``having teeth'' is not sufficient for ``being a mammal'' under open-world semantics. SC produces a 6:6 split (Unknown:6, True:6) and tiebreaks alphabetically to True (wrong). SICA extracts 7 constraints; MaxSAT excludes 1 constraint inconsistent with the rest, reducing the weighted score for True-voting traces and tipping the aggregation to Unknown (correct). The excluded constraint likely captured an incorrect inference step (e.g., affirming the consequent) present only in True-voting traces. While SICA succeeds here, the success is coincidental: the excluded constraint happens to anti-correlate with the correct answer.
280	
281	\paragraph{Case 2: SC Wins (ProofWriter-1066\_Q6, ProofWriter).}
282	
283	\emph{Key chain}: White(Bob)$\to$Round(Bob) [white things are round] $\to$ Young(Bob) [all round things are young]. \emph{Conclusion}: ``Bob is not young.'' \emph{Gold}: False (Bob IS young).
284	
285	SC produces a 6:6 split (False:6, True:6) and tiebreaks to False (correct). SICA extracts 17 constraints; MaxSAT excludes 2 that appear preferentially in False-voting traces. These excluded constraints likely captured correct intermediate derivations (e.g., \texttt{young\_bob == True}) that appeared only in traces completing the full deduction chain. By excluding them, MaxSAT removes evidence supporting the correct answer. SICA selects True (wrong). This case illustrates how self-extracted constraints can systematically mislead: correct reasoning steps become discriminative signals that the solver mistakenly penalizes.
286	
287	\paragraph{Case 3: Non-discriminative Constraints (ProofWriter-903\_Q6, ProofWriter).}
288	
289	\emph{Key chain}: Nice(Mouse)$\to$Cold(Mouse) [all nice people are cold] $\to$ Chases(Mouse,Mouse) [nice and cold $\to$ chase mouse]. \emph{Conclusion}: ``The mouse does not chase the mouse.'' \emph{Gold}: False.
290	
291	SC produces a 6:6 split (False:6, Unknown:6) and tiebreaks to False (correct). SICA extracts 44 constraints but excludes only 1 (2.3\%). The remaining 43 are domain facts and grounded rules (\texttt{nice\_mouse == True}, \texttt{Implies(nice\_mouse, cold\_mouse)}, etc.) that Z3 satisfies identically regardless of the final answer. Both False-voting and Unknown-voting traces share the same premises and grounded rules; they differ only in whether the trace completed the full derivation chain. The single excluded constraint carries negligible weight against 43 shared constraints, so SICA collapses to SC.
292	
293	\paragraph{Pattern.}
294	
295	These cases exemplify the general pattern across the 773 agreeing problems: the vast majority of extracted constraints encode shared domain structure rather than answer-specific reasoning, and MaxSAT aggregation degenerates to majority vote. Table~\ref{tab:case_summary} summarizes.

316	
317	ProofWriter problems encode deductive rules as Domain-Specific Language (DSL) logic programs. Each problem uses one of four predicate subtypes: attribute predicates with or without negation (AttNeg, AttNoneg), and relation predicates with or without negation (RelNeg, RelNoneg). Relation predicates involve binary relations between entities (e.g., \texttt{eats(bear, squirrel)}), while attribute predicates assign unary properties (e.g., \texttt{kind(anne)}).

Of the 600 ProofWriter problems, 594 (99.0\%) produce valid Z3 parses; the remaining 6 fail due to unsupported DSL constructs. Across all 7{,}128 trace-problem pairs submitted to Z3, the solver returns a result in every case (0\% solver errors). Z3 evaluations agree with ground-truth labels on 577 of 594 parseable problems (97.14\%), confirming that the deterministic DSL-to-Z3 translation faithfully preserves problem semantics.

Relation-predicate subtypes show substantially larger gains than attribute-predicate subtypes: RelNeg improves by $+17.86$~pp and RelNoneg by $+13.01$~pp, compared to $+9.09$~pp for AttNoneg and $+6.87$~pp for AttNeg. Relation predicates involve longer reasoning chains with more intermediate entities, producing greater answer diversity across traces ($C_0$) and more opportunities for oracle constraints to correct errors.

391	\section{Extraction Error Taxonomy}
392	\label{app:extraction}
393	\label{sec:extraction-taxonomy}
394	
395	Constraints must discriminate between candidate answers for MAX-SAT to produce a ranking different from majority vote. We measure discriminative power at two levels on Qwen2.5-14B across FOLIO and ProofWriter ($n = 804$). At the source-trace level, 39.2\% of total constraint weight originates from traces whose answer differs from the plurality, but only 12.1\% of individual constraints fall into this minority category. At the Z3 semantic level, 91.8\% of constraints [95\% CI: 91.2, 92.4] are technically discriminative, producing different satisfiability outcomes when evaluated against different candidate answers. Only 8.2\% are non-discriminative.
396	
397	The high discriminative rate does not translate into accuracy gains because discrimination mirrors the model's own answer distribution. Each trace produces constraints with its own variable names, so Z3 treats identically-intended propositions as unrelated symbols; among cross-answer constraint pairs, 56.4\% share zero Z3 variables. This variable isolation means constraints from different traces are trivially jointly satisfiable, and MAX-SAT retains nearly all of them regardless of source answer. Removing the 8.2\% non-discriminative constraints yields zero accuracy improvement. The discriminative majority does not provide independent signal; it reinforces the majority answer that SC would already select. This confirmation bias, not a lack of discrimination, explains why SICA degenerates to majority voting (Appendix~\ref{app:ablation}).

406	
407	Figure~\ref{fig:k-sensitivity} shows SICA $\Delta$ as a function of the number of sampled traces $K$ for Mistral-7B on FOLIO ($n = 204$, seed 42). The relationship is non-monotonic: $K = 4$ yields $\Delta = -1.47$\,pp, $K = 8$ yields $\Delta = -1.96$\,pp, $K = 12$ reaches $\Delta = +3.43$\,pp, $K = 16$ drops to $\Delta = +1.47$\,pp, and $K = 20$ partially recovers to $\Delta = +1.96$\,pp. The recovery at $K = 20$ rules out a simple peaked pattern, but $K = 12$ remains the only setting with $\Delta > 2$\,pp ($p = 0.092$, marginal).

409	The apparent $\Delta$ peak at $K = 12$ is confounded with SC baseline. SICA absolute accuracy plateaus at 59.31\% (121/204) for $K \geq 12$: identical at $K = 12$ and $K = 20$. The $\Delta$ variation across these settings is driven primarily by SC fluctuations rather than by SICA improvement. $K = 12$ produces a relatively low SC (55.88\%), placing it in the intermediate-SC region; $K = 8$ (SC $= 58.33\%$) and $K = 20$ (SC $= 57.35\%$) have higher baselines, compressing $\Delta$ even though SICA accuracy does not change for $K \geq 12$. Additional traces beyond $K = 12$ provide no benefit to SICA absolute performance, consistent with the constraint quality bottleneck. The $K = 12$ $\Delta$ captures only 24.1\% of the oracle ceiling ($+14.22$\,pp).

50	\paragraph{Method-level interventions.} Three method-level strategies target different aspects of the independence bottleneck on Mistral-7B (Table~\ref{tab:method_interventions}). Independent Constraint Generation (ICG) bypasses trace-constraint coupling by generating constraints directly from the problem statement, producing near-zero average effect ($\Delta = -1.96$\,pp and $+1.47$\,pp across two FOLIO seeds; $-0.50$\,pp on LogiQA; McNemar $p = .206$, n.s.). Contrastive scoring generates pro and con constraints for each candidate but yields $\Delta = -9.31$\,pp on FOLIO ($p < 0.01$) and $-4.50$\,pp on LogiQA ($p = .160$, n.s.), with ${\sim}$21\% degenerate scores on both datasets; all 34 discordant questions produced non-degenerate scores (vs.\ 20.1\% degenerate in the full sample), indicating that scoring failures stem from systematic pro-bias rather than missing constraints (Appendix~\ref{app:error-categorization}). Debate adds a proposer-critic-defense chain, producing $\Delta = -18.63$\,pp on FOLIO and $-23.00$\,pp on LogiQA, both statistically significant by McNemar's test ($p < 0.001$ on both datasets). Discordant-pair analysis reveals the asymmetry: on FOLIO, 60 questions flipped from correct to wrong versus only 22 from wrong to correct; on LogiQA, 64 versus 18. Debate failures occur not when the debate process breaks down but when it succeeds: discordant questions average 2.93 effective debate rounds vs.\ 2.52 for concordant ones, suggesting that more extensive same-model debate produces more confident but incorrect constraints. Three of six method-dataset conditions reach significance, confirming that degradation is systematic, not stochastic. Only 15 of 79 unique discordant questions overlap between Debate and Contrastive (Jaccard $= 0.19$), confirming that the two methods attack different vulnerability types while sharing a common root cause in the independence bottleneck (Appendix~\ref{app:error-categorization}). At the 7B scale, multi-role prompting adds cognitive overhead that degrades both reasoning and extraction quality.

Only 15 of 79 unique discordant questions overlap between Debate and Contrastive (Jaccard $= 0.19$), confirming that the two methods attack different vulnerability types while sharing a common root cause in the independence bottleneck (Appendix~\ref{app:error-categorization}). At the 7B scale, multi-role prompting adds cognitive overhead that degrades both reasoning and extraction quality.

Constraints extracted from wrong traces encode incorrect reasoning as formal rules. Z3 treats these rules as soft clauses with weight proportional to their frequency, so the solver preferentially satisfies the wrong constraints and penalizes traces that happen to reach the correct answer. Mistral-7B on ProofWriter ($\Delta = -2.83$\,pp, $p = 0.014$) demonstrates this effect: SICA converts a weak positive signal in trace diversity into a net negative by formalizing the errors.

+Table~\ref{tab:constraint_quality} compares constraint quality metrics across the three method-level interventions on Mistral-7B FOLIO ($n = 204$). Standard SICA extracts from reasoning traces and achieves the highest parse rate (97.1\%) but also the highest redundancy (42.9\%): nearly half of all constraints are syntactic duplicates across the 12 traces, quantifying the co-sourcing effect of same-model generation. ICG generates constraints directly from the problem statement without trace conditioning. Its lower parse rate (74.6\%) reflects the difficulty of standalone formalization at the 7B scale, though successfully parsed constraints compile at a higher rate (99.4\% vs.\ 96.5\%). ICG produces fewer unique constraints per question (24.9 vs.\ 39.3) with lower redundancy (32.3\%), consistent with the absence of trace-level repetition. Contrastive scoring generates pro and con constraint sets for each candidate answer. The format yields far fewer unique constraints per question (9.2) with zero redundancy (each pro/con pair is structurally distinct), but 62.7\% of constraints are trivially satisfied by Z3---they impose no logical tension and cannot discriminate between candidates. Only 51.0\% of Contrastive constraints are discriminative, compared to 81.4\% for standard SICA and 77.0\% for ICG.

50	\paragraph{Method-level interventions.} Three method-level strategies target different aspects of the independence bottleneck on Mistral-7B (Table~\ref{tab:method_interventions}). Independent Constraint Generation (ICG) bypasses trace-constraint coupling by generating constraints directly from the problem statement, but achieves only 74.6\% parse rate (vs.\ 97.1\% for trace-conditioned SICA; Appendix~\ref{app:constraint-quality}), reflecting limited standalone formalization capability at the 7B scale. ICG produces near-zero average effect ($\Delta = -1.96$\,pp and $+1.47$\,pp across two FOLIO seeds; $-0.50$\,pp on LogiQA; McNemar $p = .206$, n.s.). Contrastive scoring generates pro and con constraints for each candidate but yields $\Delta = -9.31$\,pp on FOLIO ($p < 0.01$) and $-4.50$\,pp on LogiQA ($p = .160$, n.s.), with ${\sim}$21\% degenerate scores on both datasets; all 34 discordant questions produced non-degenerate scores (vs.\ 20.1\% degenerate in the full sample), indicating that scoring failures stem from systematic pro-bias rather than missing constraints; 62.7\% of Contrastive constraints are trivially satisfied by Z3 (Appendix~\ref{app:constraint-quality}), explaining the degeneration mechanism (Appendix~\ref{app:error-categorization}). Debate adds a proposer-critic-defense chain, producing $\Delta = -18.63$\,pp on FOLIO and $-23.00$\,pp on LogiQA, both statistically significant by McNemar's test ($p < 0.001$ on both datasets). Discordant-pair analysis reveals the asymmetry: on FOLIO, 60 questions flipped from correct to wrong versus only 22 from wrong to correct; on LogiQA, 64 versus 18. Debate failures occur not when the debate process breaks down but when it succeeds: discordant questions average 2.93 effective debate rounds vs.\ 2.52 for concordant ones, suggesting that more extensive same-model debate produces more confident but incorrect constraints. Three of six method-dataset conditions reach significance, confirming that degradation is systematic, not stochastic. Only 15 of 79 unique discordant questions overlap between Debate and Contrastive (Jaccard $= 0.19$), confirming that the two methods attack different vulnerability types while sharing a common root cause in the independence bottleneck (Appendix~\ref{app:error-categorization}). At the 7B scale, multi-role prompting adds cognitive overhead that degrades both reasoning and extraction quality.
